courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming I
courses.description: Java-based introduction to objects, classes, and unit tests.

courses.title: Object-Oriented Programming II
courses.description: Data structures, generics, and a larger team project.

courses.title: Computer Systems
courses.description: C, pointers, memory, and how a process actually runs.

courses.title: Programming in C++
courses.description: Systems-oriented C++: memory, templates, and the standard library.

courses.title: Organization of Programming Languages
courses.description: Interpreters, types, and why languages look the way they do.

courses.title: Algorithms
courses.description: Asymptotics, graphs, and the proofs behind common algorithms.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, derivatives, and the first pass at modeling change.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration techniques and sequences that do not always cooperate.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector spaces, matrices, and the linear maps behind data and graphics.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Multivariable calculus in R3, with an eye toward physics.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: First-order systems and the models they show up in.

courses.title: Applications of Linear Algebra
courses.description: Least squares, spectral ideas, and computation over theory.

courses.title: Advanced Calculus
courses.description: Epsilon-delta analysis for students heading toward graduate work.

courses.title: Intro to Psychology
courses.description: A first survey of mind, brain, development, and social behavior.

courses.title: Statistical Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Descriptive stats, inference, and how psychologists lie with graphs.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Attitudes, groups, and the situations that change what people do.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Design, measurement, and writing a study you could actually run.

courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: Attention, memory, and the limits of what we notice.

courses.title: Adult Psychopathology
courses.description: Major disorders, diagnostic debates, and treatment overviews.

courses.title: Data Science for Psychology
courses.description: Cleaning behavioral data and reporting it without overclaiming.

courses.title: American History to 1865
courses.description: Colonies, constitution, and the road to the Civil War.

courses.title: American History since 1865
courses.description: Reconstruction through the late twentieth century.

courses.title: Western Civilization
courses.description: A survey from the ancient Mediterranean to industrial Europe.

courses.title: Survey of East Asia
courses.description: China, Japan, and Korea from early empires to the modern state.

courses.title: Europe in the 20th Century
courses.description: War, welfare states, and the long aftermath of 1945.

courses.title: The Age of Revolutions
courses.description: Atlantic revolutions and the political vocabulary they left behind.

courses.title: History of Science
courses.description: Instruments, institutions, and how scientific authority is made.

courses.title: Academic Writing
courses.description: Argument, revision, and citing sources without drowning in them.

courses.title: Introduction to Literature
courses.description: Close reading across poetry, drama, and short fiction.

courses.title: American Literature
courses.description: From early national writing to the postwar novel.

courses.title: Creative Writing
courses.description: Workshops on fiction and nonfiction, with weekly drafts.

courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: Five plays, the sonnets, and how performance changes a text.

courses.title: Modernist Fiction
courses.description: Joyce, Woolf, Faulkner, and the sentence as experiment.

courses.title: Digital Rhetoric
courses.description: How argument works when the page is a feed.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Physics I
courses.description: Mechanics with calculus. Labs included.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Physics II
courses.description: Electricity, magnetism, and an introduction to waves.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: Python for physicists who need to plot before they prove.

courses.title: Experimental Physics
courses.description: Error analysis, instruments, and writing a lab that another person can repeat.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods
courses.description: Complex analysis and special functions as tools, not destinations.

courses.title: Quantum Physics I
courses.description: The Schrödinger equation and the first exactly solvable systems.

courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Proofs, counting, graphs, and the discrete math CS actually uses.

courses.title: Introduction to Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Ensembles, entropy, and why temperature is a Lagrange multiplier.
